root_cause: In Console.print, when a style= argument is given, the styled branch calls Segment.apply_style(render(renderable), style) over ALL rendered segments, including the trailing '\n' segment that Text emits as its end. With soft_wrap=False the later Segment.split_and_crop_lines pass re-splits on newlines and emits an unstyled Segment.line(), which hides the bug. With soft_wrap=True the buffer is extended with new_segments directly, so the newline itself carries the background style. The output is '\x1b[34;47mtext\x1b[0m\x1b[34;47m\n\x1b[0m', and a terminal that scrolls fills the new line with the background color.
best_solution:
Style the text of each line but never the newline. Add a classmethod Segment.split_lines_terminator(segments) next to Segment.split_lines. It yields (line_segments, had_newline) tuples: it partitions non-control segment text on '
', yields (line, True) at each newline and a final (line, False) if anything remains. In the styled branch of Console.print, compute render_style = self.get_style(style) and new_line = Segment.line() once. For each rendered line, extend with Segment.apply_style(line, render_style), then append the unstyled new_line if had_newline. The output for soft_wrap then matches the soft_wrap=False path: the reset comes before '
'. How to get there from the statement: run the issue's repro with soft_wrap on and off, diff the ANSI output, and see that the only difference is a styled '
'. Then find the branch where the soft_wrap path skips the line re-splitting the other path does.

tests/test_segment.py::test_split_lines_terminator: list(Segment.split_lines_terminator([Segment('Hello
World')])) == [([Segment('Hello')], True), ([Segment('World')], False)]. tests/test_segment.py::test_split_lines_terminator_single_line: [Segment('Hello')] -> [([Segment('Hello')], False)]. tests/test_text.py::test_soft_wrap_styled: Console(color_system='standard', width=80, force_terminal=True); print('soft wrap is on', style='blue on white', soft_wrap=True) then print('Next line') must capture exactly '\x1b[34;47msoft wrap is on\x1b[0m
Next line
' (no padding, no styled newline). Two of the three tests need an exact new classmethod name and a (list, bool) tuple return shape that appears nowhere in the statement or the linked issue.
locating_signals: The statement is only the title 'fix background style with soft wrap' plus a bare issue URL. The keywords 'soft wrap' and 'style' point to Console.print in rich/console.py, where the soft_wrap parameter and the style=/apply_style branch both live (grep 'soft_wrap' and 'apply_style'). No gold function is named. The new Segment.split_lines_terminator helper cannot be found from the text; only its sibling Segment.split_lines hints at the naming pattern.
our_outcome_summary: All four configs failed in the Kaggle env (v4/v6/v7/v8 kaggle_env_pass false). v4 (196 s, 71 calls) added only scratch files (reproduce_issue.py, test_soft_wrap_fix.py) and no source change; its notes show it could not see the issue and guessed wrongly that terminal wrapping should keep the background. v6 (96 s, 50 calls) added an elif soft_wrap branch that runs Segment.split_and_crop_lines(width, pad=True). This crops and pads to console width, which breaks soft_wrap's no-crop meaning and the exact-output test, although it does separate out the newline. v7 (300 s, 100 calls, hit the call cap) did the reverse of the fix: it padded each line to self.width using the last segment's style, spreading the background further. v8 (180 s, 79 calls) produced an empty patch. None added Segment.split_lines_terminator, so both test_segment tests fail with AttributeError even for a behaviorally correct console fix.
generalizable_lesson: When the statement is only a title plus an issue link you cannot open, rebuild the bug yourself. Write a 3-line repro that exercises the named flag, print repr() of the raw output with the flag on and off, and treat the flag-off output as the spec. Look for escape codes or styling leaking onto separators like '\n'. The fix is usually in the branch that skips a normalization step the other branch performs. Do not add padding, cropping or extra output: hidden tests compare exact strings. When you need a helper, put it on the class that owns the data type, next to its closest sibling, with a name extending the sibling's (split_lines -> split_lines_<variant>), because hidden tests often unit-test the helper directly.
acceptable_alternatives: The console behavior (test_soft_wrap_styled) can be fixed several ways. You can split the rendered segments with Segment.split_lines and re-insert unstyled Segment.line(), taking care not to add a newline where the render had none. You can filter segments so apply_style skips any segment whose text is '\n'. Or you can split each segment on '\n' inline in Console.print. Any of these passes the console test, but the two test_segment.py tests also require exactly Segment.split_lines_terminator returning (list[Segment], bool) tuples, with a trailing (line, False) only when text remains after the last newline.
